title: Shokz
desc: Bone conduction and open-ear headphones and headsets

pages.t: Shokz makes headphones that leave your ears open, so you hear music or calls and the world around you. The company dates from 2004, launched its first headphones in 2011 as AfterShokz, and renamed itself Shokz in 2021.
g: Open-ear
Headphones that do not seal or plug the ear canal, so outside sound still reaches you.

pages.t: Shokz says it sells in more than 60 countries and regions, including through retailers such as Costco, Best Buy and MediaMarkt. It also claims over 20 million units sold. These are the company's own numbers, but they point to a real, mature brand.

The range has three groups: sports headphones, workout and lifestyle earbuds and communication headsets for calls and the office. There are also accessories such as charging cables. One idea ties it all together: stay aware of your surroundings.

quiz.q: What was Shokz called before 2021?
quiz.w: The brand started as AfterShokz and adopted the Shokz name in 2021.

quiz.q: What idea ties the Shokz range together?
o: Hearing music while staying aware of your surroundings
quiz.w: Every Shokz line leaves the ear open so you can still hear what is around you.

quiz.q: Which is one of the three main Shokz product groups?
quiz.w: Communication headsets for calls and offices sit beside sports headphones and lifestyle earbuds.

src.l: Shokz: how bone conduction headphones work

pages.t: Normal headphones push sound down the ear canal to the eardrum. Bone conduction turns sound into tiny vibrations that travel through the skin and skull bone straight to the inner ear. The ear canal stays completely open.
g: Cochlea
The snail-shaped part of the inner ear that turns vibrations into signals for the brain.
Transducer
The small part that turns the electrical audio signal into vibrations.

pages.t: Shokz uses two methods. Bone conduction headphones rest on the cheekbone. Open-ear earbuds instead send sound through the air from a small speaker near the ear canal, with no seal or ear tip. Both leave your ears free.
g: Air conduction
Normal hearing: sound travels through the air into the ear.

pages.t: Shokz's DualPitch combines the two: a bone conduction driver handles mids and highs, and a separate air conduction driver handles bass with minimal vibration. Shokz presents this as the reason newer models sound fuller.
g: Driver
The speaker unit inside a headphone.
Mids and highs
Voices and instruments, as opposed to deep bass.

quiz.q: How does bone conduction deliver sound?
o: Through vibrations in the skull to the inner ear
Through radio waves to the brain
quiz.w: The transducer vibrates, and the vibrations travel through the bone to the cochlea.

quiz.q: How do open-ear earbuds like OpenFit deliver sound?
o: Through the air from a speaker near the ear canal
quiz.w: They use air conduction without sealing the ear, so they are not bone conduction.

quiz.q: What does DualPitch do?
o: Splits audio between two Bluetooth devices
Uses a bone conduction driver for mids and highs plus an air driver for bass
quiz.w: DualPitch pairs two drivers so bass comes from air, with less buzzing vibration.

pages.t: OpenRun Pro 2 is the flagship sports model: DualPitch sound, up to 12 hours of playback, USB-C charging and IP55 for sweat and splashes. It comes in standard and mini sizes. OpenRun Air 2 is a lightweight option, and OpenMove is described by Shokz as budget-friendly.
g: IP55
A rating for dust and water protection. IP55 handles sweat and splashes, not swimming.

pages.t: OpenSwim Pro is rated IP68 and can go 2 metres deep in fresh water. It has 32 GB of built-in MP3 storage. Bluetooth works on land, but water blocks Bluetooth, so it switches to MP3 mode underwater.

OpenRun Pro 2 is not meant for swimming or showering. Shokz also advises keeping volume low enough to hear traffic, and warns that headphones while cycling or driving can seriously impair hearing it. Open ears help, but they are not a safety guarantee.

quiz.q: Which Shokz model has built-in MP3 storage for swimming?
quiz.w: OpenSwim Pro switches to MP3 mode underwater because Bluetooth does not work well in water.

quiz.q: A customer wants to wear OpenRun Pro 2 in the pool. What do you say?
o: No, it is IP55 and not meant for swimming; suggest OpenSwim Pro
quiz.w: IP55 covers sweat and splashes only.

quiz.q: Which line is the Shokz flagship for running?
quiz.w: OpenRun Pro 2 is listed as the flagship sports model with DualPitch sound.

pages.t: The OpenFit 2 series are earbuds that rest outside the ear canal, held by a flexible ear hook. Each weighs 9.4 g. Battery is up to 11 hours, or 48 hours with the case, and the rating is IP55. The OpenFit 2+ adds Qi wireless charging and Dolby Audio.
g: Qi
The common standard for wireless charging pads.

pages.t: OpenDots 2 clip onto the ear instead of hooking over it. Each earbud weighs 6.4 g, battery is up to 10 hours (40 with the case) and the rating is IP57. Either earbud works on either ear. Siblings include the very light OpenFit Air 2 and the clip-on OpenDots Air.

These are air conduction, not bone conduction. DirectPitch aims sound at the ear and limits leakage. Dual microphones with AI help voices on calls, but there is no active noise cancellation, and outside sound is never blocked.
g: ANC
Active noise cancelling: electronics that cancel outside noise.
Beamforming
Microphones focusing on your voice and ignoring other directions.

quiz.q: Which design clips onto the ear?
quiz.w: OpenDots 2 uses a clip-on design; OpenFit uses an ear hook.

quiz.q: Do OpenFit 2 earbuds have active noise cancellation?
o: No, they are open-ear and do not block outside sound
quiz.w: Their dual microphones clean up your voice on calls, but they do not cancel outside noise.

quiz.q: What extra does OpenFit 2+ add over the base OpenFit 2?
o: Qi wireless charging and Dolby Audio
quiz.w: Shokz lists Qi wireless charging and Dolby Audio for the 2+ model only.

pages.t: OpenMeet2 is a bone conduction headset for all-day office comfort: 77.9 g, flip-to-mute boom mic, red busy light and up to 12 hours of talk time. OpenComm2 is lighter at 35 g, with a rotatable boom mic and up to 16 hours of talk time. Both are open-ear.

UC versions come bundled with the Loop120 wireless adapter for a PC or Mac. Shokz says the adapter gives a more stable connection than Bluetooth. Standard OpenMeet2 has no adapter and connects by Bluetooth only, though the adapter is sold as an accessory.
g: UC
Unified communications: calls, chat and video meetings in one set of apps.
Dongle
A small USB adapter that links a wireless headset to a computer.

pages.t: On OpenComm2 the noise cancelling is for the microphone, so callers hear you more clearly. It does not silence the room for you. OpenMeet2 uses dual AI microphones; Shokz claims up to 99.4% background noise reduction, but real results vary.

quiz.q: What does the UC version add?
quiz.w: UC bundles the headset with the Loop120 adapter.

quiz.q: Which headset weighs about 35 g with a rotatable boom mic?
quiz.w: OpenComm2 is the lighter headset with a boom mic.

quiz.q: A customer asks if OpenComm2 cancels the noise around the wearer. Best answer?
o: Its noise cancelling is for the microphone so callers hear you clearly
Yes, full active noise cancelling for the listener
quiz.w: Shokz describes microphone noise filtering, not noise cancelling for what you hear.

pages.t: Runner or outdoor athlete: OpenRun Pro 2, or OpenRun Air 2 for lighter weight. Swimmer: OpenSwim Pro. Gym-goer who prefers earbuds: OpenFit 2 series. Commuter or traveller who wants something small: OpenDots 2, clipped on and light.

Long calls at a desk: OpenMeet2 UC for all-day comfort. Mobile or hybrid worker, light and on the move: OpenComm2 UC with its boom mic. If the customer connects to a PC, usually choose the UC version with the adapter, not the Bluetooth-only one.

Ask what matters first: awareness, comfort, call clarity or water. Awareness and comfort point to the whole range. Call clarity points to a boom mic or dual AI mics. Water points to OpenSwim Pro. Loud, noisy places point away from open-ear.

quiz.q: A swimmer wants music in the pool. Which?
quiz.w: OpenSwim Pro has IP68 and MP3 mode for underwater use.

quiz.q: A hybrid worker on a PC wants all-day comfort for long meetings. Which fits?
quiz.w: OpenMeet2 UC is built for all-day office comfort and comes with the Loop120 adapter.

quiz.q: A customer takes calls on the move and wants a very light headset with a boom mic. Which?
quiz.w: OpenComm2 is 35 g with a rotatable boom mic.

quiz.q: Which need should make you think twice about open-ear?
o: Blocking noise in a very loud workplace
quiz.w: Open-ear cannot isolate the wearer from loud surroundings the way sealed ANC headphones can.

src.l: Shokz guide: open-ear for Zoom and Teams

pages.t: In-ear earbuds and ANC headphones seal or cancel the world out. Shokz itself says sealed noise-cancelling headphones block more in very loud settings. If a customer wants isolation on a plane or a noisy factory floor, those are the better tool.
g: In-ear
Earbuds with tips that sit inside the ear canal.
Isolation
How much outside noise is kept out.

pages.t: Open-ear keeps you aware of your surroundings. Shokz says it also reduces ear fatigue and makes your own voice sound more natural on calls. It suits home offices, kitchen tables and open-plan floors, where hearing colleagues matters.

Usually treat Shokz as a different category, not a rival to sealed in-ear products. Trade-offs: less isolation and possible sound leakage at high volume. Wikipedia notes bone conduction users can still be less aware than with no headphones at all.

quiz.q: When do sealed ANC headphones beat open-ear?
o: Very loud places where isolation matters
quiz.w: Shokz admits sealed noise-cancelling headphones block more in very loud settings.

quiz.q: Which is a benefit Shokz claims for open-ear?
quiz.w: Shokz says open ears reduce ear fatigue and make your own voice sound natural.

quiz.q: A customer works on an open-plan floor and wants to hear colleagues while on calls. Pitch?
quiz.w: Open-ear lets them hear the room, which suits open-plan work.

src.l: Shokz guide: open-ear for Zoom and Teams

pages.t: A certified headset has been tested by a meeting-app provider such as Zoom, Webex or Microsoft, so it should work with that app's buttons and features out of the box. Customers with IT rules often ask for it, so know the exact status before you promise.
g: Certified
Tested and approved by the app provider for that headset model.

pages.t: Shokz's own pages say OpenMeet2 UC is certified for Zoom and Webex, and OpenComm2 UC is Zoom certified. We did not find a Microsoft Teams certification claim on those pages. Some resellers list Teams, so verify per model and version.

Shokz setup guidance names Microsoft Teams as an app you can use with its adapter. That is a different claim from certification. Never say Teams certified unless the current Shokz or Microsoft listing for that exact model says so. When unsure, ask your distributor contact.

quiz.q: Which meeting apps does Shokz list for OpenMeet2 UC certification?
quiz.w: Shokz lists Zoom and Webex for OpenMeet2 UC.

quiz.q: A buyer needs Microsoft Teams certification. What is the right move?
o: Confirm the status for that exact model first
Say yes, it works with Teams
quiz.w: Works with Teams is not the same as certified, and the Shokz pages did not claim it.

quiz.q: What does certification mean?
o: The app provider tested it for that headset
quiz.w: Certification means the app provider tested and approved the model.

pages.t: Shokz offers Shokz Connect (PC software), the Shokz App for phones, and Command Center, a portal for managing devices across an organisation and rolling out settings and updates. The business page also lists Contact Sales, Find a Reseller and a Partner Portal.
g: Deployment
Rolling a product out to many users at once.

pages.t: Shokz.com says every order comes with a 2-year warranty. Reseller terms may differ, so check with your distributor contact. Shokz also says water resistance can fade with normal wear, and OpenMeet2 is not water-resistant at all.

Accessories include charging cables (a magnetic cable for OpenRun, a data cable for OpenSwim Pro), a drawstring carry bag, a gift bag and the Roadwave Lens. OpenRun Pro 2 comes in standard and mini, which helps smaller heads fit comfortably.

quiz.q: Which tool lets IT manage many Shokz headsets centrally?
quiz.w: Shokz lists Command Center for centralised management of deployments.

quiz.q: Which Shokz headset is not water-resistant?
quiz.w: Shokz states OpenMeet2 is not water-resistant.

quiz.q: What can help a customer with a small head fit OpenRun Pro 2?
quiz.w: OpenRun Pro 2 comes in standard and mini sizes.

src.l: Shokz guide: open-ear for Zoom and Teams

pages.t: Customers used to sealed headphones may find open-ear less rich. Be honest: you trade some isolation for awareness and comfort. Shokz's answer is DualPitch, with an air driver for bass. Position it as a lifestyle and safety choice, not as studio sound.

Shokz says bone conduction reduces sound spreading through the air, and it names LeakSlayer 3.0 on OpenMeet2 and DirectPitch on earbuds. It publishes no measured figures here, and its own guide notes leakage is possible at high volume. Suggest a demo in a quiet office.
g: Leakage
Sound escaping so people nearby can hear it.

pages.t: Bass is the classic worry. DualPitch routes bass through an air driver. OpenRun Pro 2 has a Bass Boost EQ mode and OpenDots 2 has a Bass preset. Set expectations: tuned bass is possible, but do not promise the thump of sealed over-ear headphones.
g: EQ
Equaliser: settings that boost or cut parts of the sound, like bass or voices.

quiz.q: A customer says Shokz will annoy colleagues with leakage. Best reply?
o: Shokz works to limit it, but it can occur at high volume, so try a demo
quiz.w: Shokz makes leakage claims without published figures and admits leakage at high volume.

quiz.q: What is Shokz's answer to the bass worry on newer models?
o: A separate air driver for bass
quiz.w: DualPitch sends bass through an air conduction driver.

quiz.q: How should you position Shokz against audiophile headphones?
o: As lifestyle and awareness, not studio sound
As the best sound at any price
quiz.w: Honest positioning builds trust: the draw is awareness and comfort.

lessons.title: Questions to ask and traps to avoid

src.l: Shokz guide: open-ear for Zoom and Teams

pages.t: Ask: where will it be used, how many hours of calls a day, which meeting app, PC or phone, how many users, and does IT need central management. The answers separate sports, office and everyday customers quickly.

Do not promise Teams certified without checking. Do not sell OpenRun Pro 2 for swimming. Do not offer OpenMeet2 where water is a risk. Do not pitch open-ear for a very loud factory floor. Check that PC users get a UC or adapter version.

Open ears help people hear traffic, but Shokz advises keeping volume low and warns that headphones while cycling or driving can seriously impair hearing it. Wikipedia does not claim bone conduction protects hearing. Never promise hearing protection or safety.

quiz.q: Which is a good first discovery question?
o: Which meeting app do you use and how long are your calls?
How many units can you take?
quiz.w: Meeting app and call length quickly point to the right model.

quiz.q: A customer asks if Shokz protects their hearing. Best answer?
o: No claim: keep volume low and stay aware
quiz.w: The sources do not claim hearing protection, so never promise it.

quiz.q: A customer needs headphones for a very loud workshop. Best advice?
o: Warn that open-ear gives little isolation and consider sealed protection
quiz.w: Open-ear leaves noise in by design.

about: Open-ear audio specialist. The company dates from 2004 and was called AfterShokz until 2021. Makes bone conduction headphones, open-ear earbuds and headsets for calls.
Sells to runners and active people and to office and hybrid workers. Shokz says it sells in more than 60 countries and regions.
Different because the ear canal stays open, so you hear music, calls and the world around you. It isolates less than sealed or noise-cancelling headphones.
